welcome.eyebrow: A NASA Space Apps Challenge Story
welcome.title: NovoSriti
welcome.subtitle: Abandoned, but not forgotten.
welcome.description: Every piece of equipment has a story. Some are still waiting to be heard.

prologue.title: What remains after we leave?
prologue.description: Humans have explored the Moon and Mars, leaving machines and instruments behind. They may be silent now, but their stories are still part of exploration.

chapters.title: The silent mirrors
chapters.description: Astronauts left special mirrors on the Moon. Scientists still send laser beams toward them to measure the distance between Earth and the Moon.
chapters.truthText: Apollo astronauts placed laser retroreflectors on the lunar surface. They are still used for scientific measurements.
chapters.question: How can a mirror help us measure the Moon?

chapters.title: Listening to the Moon
chapters.description: Apollo astronauts left instruments that listened for moonquakes. These devices helped scientists understand what happens beneath the lunar surface.
chapters.truthText: Apollo missions deployed seismometers to study seismic activity on the Moon.
chapters.question: Can the Moon have earthquakes?

chapters.title: The first visitors
chapters.description: The Viking landers reached Mars and sent back images and scientific data. They helped humans learn more about the red planet.
chapters.truthText: NASA's Viking 1 and Viking 2 landers successfully operated on the surface of Mars.
chapters.question: What did the first landers teach us about Mars?

chapters.title: The explorers that kept going
chapters.description: These twin rovers explored Mars for years. Their missions lasted far longer than originally planned, helping scientists study the planet's past.
chapters.truthText: Spirit and Opportunity were NASA Mars Exploration Rovers. Both operated far beyond their planned primary mission.
chapters.question: How long can a rover keep exploring?

chapters.title: A little helicopter, a big achievement
chapters.description: Ingenuity arrived on Mars with the Perseverance rover. It became the first aircraft to make a powered, controlled flight on another planet.
chapters.truthText: Ingenuity completed the first powered, controlled flight on another planet. Its mission ended in 2024.
chapters.question: How did a small helicopter fly on Mars?

chapters.title: A message beyond the stars
chapters.description: Voyager 1 continues its journey through interstellar space. Its story reminds us that exploration can reach far beyond the worlds we visit.
chapters.truthText: Voyager 1 launched in 1977 and became the first spacecraft to enter interstellar space.
chapters.question: How far can human curiosity travel?
